$comment: The ONE list of examples: order, titles, one-line descriptions, sections, tags, screenshots. Read by examples/_shared/shell.ts (top bar: back link, prev/next, jump menu), tools/site.mjs (landing-page cards, for both `yarn examples` and the deployed site) and tools/build-site.mjs (which example dirs deploy). Entry: { id (unique), section (a sections[].id), href (relative to the site root: '<dir>/' or '<dir>/<page>.html'), title, description (one line, plain text), tags (labels from `tags` below), shot (file in examples/site/shots, optional), deployed (built into GitHub Pages) }. To add an example: add its entry here, give it a screenshot, and call mountShell({ id }) in its entry module.

tags.runtimes: WGSL / WebNN / ONNX Runtime / HF kernels

sections.blurb: The API in a few lines, then what good input looks like.

examples.title: Hello world
examples.description: A noisy render, Denoiser.create(), denoise(), canvas. No three.js, no build tricks.

examples.title: Before / after gallery
examples.description: Pre-rendered path-traced scenes at 1 to 16 samples per pixel, denoised live: drag the divider, step the noise ladder, toggle albedo + normal.

examples.title: Aux inputs, explained
examples.description: What the network sees: albedo and normal conventions, plus three real bugs you can switch on and watch degrade the output.

examples.title: three.js path tracer
examples.description: three.js WebGPUPathTracer and the denoiser on one GPUDevice: an interactive scene, path traced progressively and denoised live.

examples.title: LDraw Eiffel Tower
examples.description: A LEGO Eiffel Tower: raster preview while you orbit, path trace and denoise when the camera comes to rest.

examples.title: Raw WebGPU
examples.description: No framework: a single-file WGSL path tracer and the denoiser sharing one GPUDevice. The copy-paste integration recipe.

examples.title: Babylon.js
examples.description: Babylon renders, the denoiser cleans it: over a timed CPU round trip between two devices, or zero-copy on Babylon's own GPUDevice.

examples.title: Ray-traced shadows & reflections in a raster app
examples.description: A three.js raster scene that traces two effects at 1 ray per pixel, denoised every frame by ffxShadows() / ffxReflections(), vs shadow maps and env maps.

examples.title: Reflections, explained: probe, SSR, ray tracing
examples.description: A guided tour of how engines find reflections (probes, SSR, ray tracing, the hybrid): split-screen comparisons of where each one breaks, a view of where every pixel's reflection comes from, and what each costs.

examples.title: Reflections in two rooms: probes, SSR and rays
examples.description: A probe per room and one in the doorway give every surface the right reflection for almost nothing; SSR and one traced ray per pixel + ffxReflections() add the moving mirror ball, contact and what the probes never saw. Lights that change colour, probes re-baked or frozen.

examples.title: Reflection probes on r186 (preview of three.js #35046)
examples.description: Ben Houston's box-projected, blended reflection probes, running on three r186 until his PR lands: two rooms, a doorway probe, same API, swap in his when it ships.

examples.title: Baked + dynamic shadows: when to split
examples.description: Bake what never moves (a lightmap, denoised once with OIDN, or a world-space cache), trace only the moving objects every frame with FFX: what the split buys, what it costs, and when to use it.

examples.title: Realtime shadows: ours vs FidelityFX (experimental)
examples.description: The ray-traced shadows scene, 1 ray per pixel, split-screen: ffxShadows() against realtimeShadows(), the penumbra-aware ShadowDenoiser of denoiser/realtime.

examples.title: Realtime GI, reflections and AO (experimental)
examples.description: The same scene lit only by 1-ray signals: realtimeDiffuseSpecular() on a traced diffuse bounce and three's stochastic SSR, realtimeOcclusion() for AO, split-screen against the raw signal and ffxReflections().

examples.title: three.js SSR: FidelityFX vs recurrentDenoise
examples.description: three's SSR denoise example with the ffxReflections() TSL node swapped in, split-screen against three's own denoiser.

examples.title: FidelityFX shadows & reflections
examples.description: AMD's FidelityFX denoisers ported to WGSL: 1-sample ray-traced signals denoised every frame vs a converged reference.

examples.title: Realtime vs OIDN
examples.description: Noisy SSR denoised two ways: three's temporal recurrentDenoise every frame vs OIDN single-image denoising on a cadence.

examples.title: Pipeline Lab
examples.description: The full offline pipeline: three-gpu-pathtracer → denoiser → @pmndrs/upscaler, every stage tweakable, with a benchmark you can run on every runtime and share.

examples.title: Benchmark
examples.description: Cold and warm timings, per-stage stats and fp16-vs-fp32 PSNR for every runtime across image sizes.

examples.title: Eval vs native OIDN
examples.description: Every OIDN RT model on every runtime and precision vs native OIDN: quality and speed.

examples.title: WGSL runtime bench
examples.description: The Denoiser facade on ORT, HF kernels and hand-written WGSL: parity and warm timings.

examples.title: WebNN bench
examples.description: The OIDN U-Net built as a WebNN graph vs the WGSL runtime: network-only timings and parity.

examples.title: HF kernels smoke test
examples.description: The OIDN U-Net op by op on @huggingface/kernels, checked against onnxruntime-web.

examples.title: ORT WebGPU smoke test
examples.description: A converted OIDN ONNX U-Net on onnxruntime-web (WebGPU EP) with zero-copy GPU-buffer IO.

examples.title: Aux split-graph check
examples.description: Verifies the ORT split-graph workaround for aux models against a WASM reference.

examples.title: Package end-to-end test
examples.description: import { Denoiser } from 'denoiser' with the default AutoRuntime, end to end.

examples.title: Upscaler wiring check (synthetic noise)
examples.description: Raster scene + injected fake noise → denoiser → @pmndrs/upscaler (FSR3 or FSR1) on one device. Checks the texture hand-offs; not path-traced input.
